name: Key Pair Generator & Converter (PEM, JWK, OpenSSH)
summary: Generate RSA, ECDSA and Ed25519 key pairs or convert keys between PEM, JWK and OpenSSH formats, with SSH fingerprints.
about: Makes key pairs in your browser with the browser's own Web Crypto generator and the audited @noble/curves and @noble/hashes libraries, and writes each one in the formats other software asks for, with the SHA256 and MD5 fingerprints that ssh-keygen prints. RSA keys are generated in a background worker so the page stays responsive, and the worker is stopped if it takes too long. Nothing you generate is sent, stored or logged: the keys exist only in this page until you close it.
supports: RSA key pairs of 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits with public exponent 65537, generated by Web Crypto in a background worker
The private key as PKCS#8 (RFC 5958) and the public key as SubjectPublicKeyInfo (RFC 5280), both as PEM
The OpenSSH public key line (RFC 4253 section 6.6) with an optional comment
SSH fingerprints in both forms ssh-keygen prints: SHA256 (unpadded Base64) and MD5 (colon-separated hex)
limits: Keys are made only by the browser's Web Crypto generator and crypto.getRandomValues; nothing else supplies randomness.
Generating an RSA key runs in the background and stops after 60 seconds with a message; Cancel stops it at once.
Private keys are shown in plain text so you can copy them; treat every private output as a secret and close the page when you are done.
RSA sizes are limited to 2048, 3072 and 4096 bits with exponent 65537, and the keys are never protected by a passphrase.
This page makes keys; pasting a key to convert it is not offered yet.
ambiguities: RSA keys are made as RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 keys, and the key file does not record what a key is used for, so the same bytes work for signing, encryption and SSH
The comment is written after the key on the OpenSSH line and is not part of the key or its fingerprint

standards.label: RFC 5280: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and CRL Profile
RFC 8017: PKCS #1: RSA Cryptography Specifications Version 2.2
RFC 4253: The Secure Shell (SSH) Transport Layer Protocol
RFC 8410: Algorithm Identifiers for Ed25519, Ed448, X25519 and X448

apiNotes: `generateRsa(bits)` asks Web Crypto for an RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 key (SHA-256, exponent 65537) and returns its PKCS#8 and SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes; `bits` must be 2048, 3072 or 4096. `keyFromGeneratedRsa(pkcs8, spki)` reads both and checks they belong together. `keyOutputs(key, { comment })` writes every output from the package's own key model, never from the engine's own export, and returns blocks of text, fingerprints, facts and warnings. Every error is a `KeyConverterError`, `DerError` or `PemError` whose message names a position and the shape of the problem and never repeats any part of a key. `readDer`, `pemBlocks` and the Base64 and hex codecs are exported from their own files for reuse.
testNotes: Node's crypto (an OpenSSL-backed implementation independent of this package) and ssh-keygen 10.2p1 are the second opinions: RSA keys generated by Web Crypto are read from their PKCS#8 and SPKI bytes and written back byte for byte, and the fingerprints of the RFC 8032 section 7.1 test public key are the values ssh-keygen printed for the same line. The DER reader and PEM scanner are tested with hostile lengths, deep nesting and 500 KiB of BEGIN lines.
